title: Best Winter Gloves UK
short: Everyday, running and mountaineering gloves compared by warmth, touchscreen use and weight.
intro: Winter gloves range from thin touchscreen-friendly liners to heavily insulated mountaineering mitts, and the right choice depends on how cold it gets and how much dexterity you need. This guide compares gloves tested by Outdoors Magic, from everyday value picks to technical winter kit.

guide.q: How warm a glove do I actually need?
guide.a: For everyday UK winter weather, a moderate-warmth touchscreen glove such as the Simond, Arc'teryx or Mammut options is usually enough. Save the heavily insulated mountaineering gloves and mitts for genuinely cold, high-altitude or long-exposure conditions.

If you need to use your phone without removing a glove, yes. Thinner gloves and those with a conductive patch on the fingertip tend to give better touch accuracy, but touchscreen fabric can add cost and slightly reduce warmth.
Gloves give more dexterity for zips, straps and phones. Mitts keep fingers together, which traps more heat, so they suit very cold or static conditions better than gloves of similar insulation.

guide.q: How do I keep winter gloves waterproof?
guide.a: Look for a genuine waterproof membrane, such as Gore-Tex, rather than just a water-resistant coating, if you expect rain or wet snow. Reproofing sprays can restore water resistance on gloves that have lost it over time.
